sov_commodity.cub: A negotiated commodity schedule gives Cuban sugar and nickel a stable Soviet market and links imports to a longer planning horizon. Delivery commitments deepen dependence on a single trading partner.
sov_commodity.partner: Cuban commodities enter a coordinated purchasing programme, supporting supply planning and Soviet influence overseas. Administering preferential terms imposes a continuing burden on the trading institutions.
sov_commodity.proposal: Havana proposes a coordinated commodity schedule, committing exports in return for a more predictable commercial relationship with the Soviet Union.

sov_industry.cub: Joint commissions coordinate imported machinery, industrial designs and technical training for Cuban production. Faster modernisation requires a larger planning and procurement administration.
sov_industry.partner: Equipment deliveries and technical exchanges broaden the market for Soviet industrial production. Engineers and training institutions carry the continuing cost of cooperation.
sov_industry.proposal: Havana proposes an industrial modernisation programme built around machinery purchases, technical exchanges and coordinated production plans.

mex_energy.cub: Regional coordination of petroleum purchases and shipping helps Cuban enterprises plan around external supply constraints. Havana accepts greater dependence on a politically exposed regional partnership.
mex_energy.partner: Mexican commercial and diplomatic institutions coordinate an energy relationship with Cuba. Export opportunities bring a continuing administrative obligation and greater involvement in Caribbean affairs.
mex_energy.proposal: Havana proposes a regional energy commission to coordinate commercial purchases and transport arrangements with Mexico.

mex_agro.cub: Agronomists and technical institutes coordinate crop research and its industrial applications with Mexican partners. The programme broadens agricultural expertise while placing new demands on public training institutions.
mex_agro.partner: Agricultural institutes exchange research and production experience with Cuba. Shared technical work supports cultivation and scientific capacity, with a continuing obligation to fund staff and training.
mex_agro.proposal: Havana proposes an agro-industrial commission linking agricultural research, technical education and production methods in both countries.

spr_nickel.cub: A commodity and machinery protocol connects Cuban nickel exports with Spanish industrial suppliers. Access to equipment and a commercial market comes with delivery commitments and closer dependence on the partner's purchasing institutions.
spr_nickel.partner: Spanish firms gain an organised channel for machinery sales and Cuban commodities. Public commercial agencies must administer the settlement and its continuing commitments.
spr_nickel.proposal: Havana proposes a commodity and machinery protocol, matching a continuing commercial relationship with purchases from Spanish industry.

spr_training.cub: Industrial institutes and Spanish suppliers coordinate training in the operation and maintenance of imported equipment. Cuban enterprises gain technical capacity while education services carry the continuing programme.
spr_training.partner: Spanish industrial and educational institutions maintain exchanges with Cuban enterprises. Commercial experience and joint technical work develop expertise while widening the partner's influence within participating institutions.
spr_training.proposal: Havana proposes a standing industrial training agreement, tying equipment maintenance and production methods to exchanges between technical institutions.

can_rail.cub: Working with Canadian suppliers able to meet applicable export requirements, Cuba links rail-equipment purchases to maintenance and technical service. Better coordination supports construction and supply, with greater dependence on foreign commercial partners.
can_rail.partner: Canadian firms obtain industrial orders and a continuing service relationship with Cuba. Commercial agencies must administer maintenance commitments and a politically sensitive export market.
can_rail.proposal: Havana proposes a rail service contract with Canadian suppliers, connecting equipment purchases to maintenance and technical support.

can_industry.cub: A purchasing commission coordinates Canadian industrial equipment and technical exchanges for Cuban enterprises. Production and research benefit, while export commitments narrow the goods available for other markets.
can_industry.partner: Canadian suppliers and technical institutions establish a continuing Cuban market. Industrial feedback and commercial opportunities accompany new commitments to training and technical cooperation.
can_industry.proposal: Havana proposes an industrial purchasing agreement combining machinery orders with a continuing programme of technical exchanges.
